dialogue.content: おはようございます。
dialogue.English: Good morning.

dialogue.content: どうぞよろしく願いいたします。
dialogue.English: Thank you for having me.

dialogue.content: いらっしゃいますか？
dialogue.English: Are you there?

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: はじめられそうですか？
dialogue.English: Can we start now?

dialogue.content: すみません　パソコンの調子が悪くて
dialogue.English: I'm sorry, my computer is acting up.

dialogue.content: 承知いたしました。何時から始められそうですか？
dialogue.English: I see. Around what time do you think we can start?

dialogue.content: その時間にまたきましょうか？
dialogue.English: Shall I come back at that time?

dialogue.content: お願いします。　最初に年齢と性別を教えていただけますか。
dialogue.English: Yes, please. To begin, could you tell me your age and gender?

dialogue.content: 大丈夫です。
dialogue.English: It's fine now.

dialogue.content: 60歳、女性です
dialogue.English: I'm a 60-year-old woman.

dialogue.content: それでは、本日の相談はどのようなことでしょうか。
dialogue.English: Alright, what would you like to discuss today?

dialogue.content: 夫の事でちょっと悩んでまして
dialogue.English: I'm a bit worried about my husband.

dialogue.content: わかりました。旦那様のことですね。具体的にお聞きしてもよろしいでしょうか。
dialogue.English: I understand. It's about your husband. May I ask for some specifics?

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。夫の様子が最近おかしくて
dialogue.English: Thank you. Lately, my husband has been acting strangely.

dialogue.content: どんな感じでおかしいのでしょうか。
dialogue.English: In what way has he been acting strangely?

dialogue.content: 物忘れがひどく、そろそろ認知症なのかもと思い、病院に言って検査をしたらやはり軽度の認知症が始まっていると
dialogue.English: He's become very forgetful, and I suspected it might be dementia. We went to the hospital for an examination, and it was confirmed that he has early-stage mild dementia.

dialogue.content: 若年性ですね
dialogue.English: It's early-onset.

dialogue.content: 夫は年下なのでまだ55歳なんですが、言動がおかしくて
dialogue.English: My husband is younger than me—he's only 55—but his speech and actions are off.

dialogue.content: 私も相談者様と近い年齢なのでよく理解できます。５５歳のころって体に変化が出始めますよね。
dialogue.English: I'm around the same age as you, so I can understand well. Around 55, the body starts to change, doesn't it?

dialogue.content: どんなことが気になりますか。
dialogue.English: What concerns you in particular?

dialogue.content: そうですよね、でも、もともと頭のいい人で回転も速かったしいまではなんだか老人のようになってしまい元気もないしかわいそうでかわいそうで、この先どうなってしまうんだろう
dialogue.English: That's true, but he was always so smart and quick-witted. Now, it's like he's become an old man. He has no energy, and I feel so sorry for him. I wonder what will happen to us from now on.

dialogue.content: 旦那様はどんなことがお好きなのでしょうか。
dialogue.English: What does your husband enjoy?

dialogue.content: もともとシステムエンジニアでパソコンが大好きなんです
dialogue.English: He was originally a systems engineer and loves computers.

dialogue.content: それも最近パソコンに向かうとフリーズしてるっているか
dialogue.English: But recently, when he's at the computer, it's like he just freezes.

dialogue.content: 大好きなパソコンが好きなのですね。夢中になれることがあっていいですね。その時はどんな感じですか。
dialogue.English: So he loves his computer. It's great that he has something he can be absorbed in. What is he like at those times?

dialogue.content: もともとですか？
dialogue.English: Do you mean before?

dialogue.content: 現在、パソコンに向かっているときは、どんな表情でしょうか。
dialogue.English: I mean now. What is his expression like when he's at the computer?

dialogue.content: 表情・・・うーん、表情はあまり見てないですけど、画面を見つめて手が止まっている感じですかね
dialogue.English: His expression... hmm. I haven't really looked at his expression, but it seems like he just stares at the screen and his hands stop.

dialogue.content: pcに向かっているときはもともとプログラムを考えているときなのであまり話しかけたりはしないですが
dialogue.English: When he's at the PC, he's usually thinking through programs, so I don't talk to him much then.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。でも夢中になれるものをお持ちなのですね。外にはでませんか。
dialogue.English: I see. But he does have something he can get absorbed in. Does he go outside?

dialogue.content: でも、それが仕事なので、、、、最近仕事にも支障が出てきていて、、、プログラマーとして生きてきた人なので他には何もできないから
dialogue.English: But that's his job... and it's started to affect his work recently. He's lived his life as a programmer, so he can't do anything else.

dialogue.content: この先どんどん認知症が進んでいったらどうやって生計を立てていけばいいのか不安で仕方がないです
dialogue.English: I can't help but feel anxious about how we'll make a living if his dementia progresses.

dialogue.content: 旦那様が奥様と一緒に外にでて新しい景色などを観て感動したりすることには、興味がありそうですか。
dialogue.English: Does he seem like he would be interested in going outside with you to see new scenery and be moved by it?

dialogue.content: どうでしょう
dialogue.English: I'm not sure.

dialogue.content: 旦那様は他にはどんな趣味がありますか。
dialogue.English: What other hobbies does your husband have?

dialogue.content: 趣味は無いです、
dialogue.English: He doesn't have any hobbies.

dialogue.content: pc一筋のひとなので
dialogue.English: He's always been all about his PC.

dialogue.content: 奥様の趣味は何でしょうか。
dialogue.English: What are your hobbies?

dialogue.content: 私の趣味は園芸です
dialogue.English: My hobby is gardening.

dialogue.content: いいですね。旦那様はそのことについてどんなことを言っていますか。
dialogue.English: That's nice. What does your husband say about that?

dialogue.content: べつになにも
dialogue.English: Nothing in particular.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。奥様から見て、旦那様はどんなことをやるといいと思いますか。
dialogue.English: I see. From your perspective, what kinds of activities do you think would be good for him?

dialogue.content: どんなこと？よくわからないです
dialogue.English: What kinds of things? I'm not really sure.

dialogue.content: 旦那様が生き生きとするためには、奥様の支えが必要だと思います。一緒にできることはどうでしょうか。
dialogue.English: I believe your support is necessary for him to feel more alive. How about something you can do together?

dialogue.content: 支えてるつもりですけど・・・
dialogue.English: I feel like I am supporting him, but...

dialogue.content: 私が支えられていないせいで主人の症状が悪化してきているのかもしれません
dialogue.English: Maybe my husband's symptoms are getting worse because I'm not supporting him enough.

dialogue.content: でも、私が主人を生き生きさせることなんてできる気がしません
dialogue.English: But I don't feel like I can make my husband feel more alive.

dialogue.content: パソコン一筋というのが気になります。他の世界を体験していただきたいなと感じます。一緒にできることがあればよいのですが…。　ゆっくりお考えになっても大丈夫です。
dialogue.English: The fact that he's all about his PC concerns me. I feel it would be good for him to experience other things. It would be nice if there were something you could do together... You can take your time to think about it.

dialogue.content: 55年もパソコン一筋で生きてきているので、、、でも植物を見るのは好きなんだと思います
dialogue.English: He's lived his life for 55 years focused solely on computers... but I think he does like looking at plants.

dialogue.content: お部屋に植物を置いてありますので
dialogue.English: We have plants in the room.

dialogue.content: いいですね。旦那様はきっと自然がお好きなのかもしれませんね。天気の良い日はどんなことをしたらよいでしょうか。
dialogue.English: That's good. Perhaps your husband likes nature. What do you think would be good to do on a nice day?

dialogue.content: 散歩に出かけてみますが、それもいつもやっています
dialogue.English: We go for walks, but we already do that regularly.

dialogue.content: その時の旦那様はどんな感じですか。
dialogue.English: How is he during those times?

dialogue.content: まあ普通ですが
dialogue.English: Well, he's just normal, I guess.

dialogue.content: いつも同じ場所に行かれるのですか。
dialogue.English: Do you always go to the same places?

dialogue.content: 色々なところにいきますよ
dialogue.English: We go to various places.

dialogue.content: 少し表情が柔らかくなるのでなるべく散歩はするようにしています
dialogue.English: His expression softens a little, so I try to make sure we go for walks as much as possible.

dialogue.content: 私も６０歳近い年齢なのですが、旦那様のことが理解できます。この年齢になるといろいろなことがあります。お医者様は、どんなことを言っていますか。
dialogue.English: I'm also close to 60, so I can understand what your husband is going through. A lot of things happen at this age. What does the doctor say?

dialogue.content: カウンセラーさんも60歳近いのですね、同世代ですね。医者はなるべく刺激を多く与えた方がいいと進めてくれました。
dialogue.English: Oh, you're close to 60 too, so we're from the same generation. The doctor recommended providing him with as much stimulation as possible.

dialogue.content: ただ、変化がありすぎるのもストレスになる場合があるので様子を見ながらと
dialogue.English: But they also said that too much change can be stressful, so to keep an eye on things as we go.

dialogue.content: その通りですね。医師の言うことを聞くことが一番だと思います。医師の言うことを聞くのはいかがでしょうか。
dialogue.English: That's exactly right. I think following the doctor's advice is best. How about doing that?

dialogue.content: はぁ、そうですか、じゃあそうします
dialogue.English: Sigh... is that so? Then I'll do that.

dialogue.content: 聞いてますけど
dialogue.English: I have been following it, though.

dialogue.content: カウンセラーは、質問をして相談者様になにか気づいてもらうことしかできないのです。医師ともう一度相談するのはいかがですか。
dialogue.English: A counselor can only ask questions and help the client realize something on their own. How about consulting with the doctor one more time?

dialogue.content: そうですね、そうします
dialogue.English: You're right, I'll do that.

dialogue.content: 医者に相談しますね
dialogue.English: I'll talk to the doctor.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。時間が迫ってきてしまいました。本日はありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: Thank you. Our time is almost up. Thank you for today.

dialogue.content: まだ時間になっていませんが、終わりなのですね？
dialogue.English: It's not time yet, but we're finishing?

dialogue.content: 結論がでましたので、時間は多少早くても大丈夫です。ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Since we've reached a conclusion, it's fine to end a little early. Thank you.

dialogue.content: 分かりました、では終了してください
dialogue.English: I understand. Please end the session then.

dialogue.content: 評価おくります
dialogue.English: I'll send my feedback.

dialogue.content: はい。
dialogue.English: Okay.
